evidence.note: Explicit up-front decomposition into ordered subsystem tasks: persistence/schema first, then REST+WS, then killable fan-out relay, then IRC, then SPA, then supervisor — dependency-correct sequencing with the seq store and fan-out transport recognized as prerequisites in the initial plan.
The broadcast-relay milestone is designed with a DB-polling fallback 'so fan-out survives' relay death — the resilience invariant is baked into the milestone design rather than bolted on later.
Foreground supervisor (respawn within 60s, survive SIGKILL) and start.sh are their own first-class milestone, matching the 8-anchor's requirement that process-supervision be designed as a milestone.
Tasks are worked in dependency order with in_progress/completed transitions (store→broadcast→http→irc→spa→supervisor), showing the milestone structure is actually followed, not just declared.

The entire REST surface (auth, workspaces, channels, messages, threads, reactions, files, search, DMs) is one coarse task rather than differentiated milestones with per-feature done-checks — limits granularity below the 8 anchor.

Highest-risk invariants (replay-across-nodes, dense seq with relay dead) are verified in a late batch rather than isolated as their own early milestones with concrete exit criteria, keeping this short of the 10 anchor.

reasoning: The agent produced an explicit, dependency-correct milestone breakdown into major subsystems (persistence→REST/WS→fan-out relay→IRC→SPA→supervisor), recognized the critical shared substrate (per-channel seq, fan-out transport with fallback) at plan time, and treated start.sh/process-supervision as a first-class milestone — clearly above anchor 5 and touching several elements of anchor 8. It falls short of a full 8-10 because the large REST surface is one undifferentiated task, done-checks are embedded implicitly in task titles rather than crisp per-milestone acceptance gates, and the riskiest cross-cutting invariants are verified in a late batch instead of being isolated as their own early milestones with exit criteria. This lands at 7.
